_purpose: Curated held-out fixture for #2753 Stage 1B / Stage 2–4 replay harness.
_schema: pair_id | claim | evidence | deberta_verdict | deberta_confidence | deberta_top_margin | llm_verdict | true_label
_true_label_source: Adjudicated ground truth (2-rater + tiebreak per Stage 3 protocol).
_gate: contradicted-class precision >= 0.95 on this set is a hard promotion block if violated

claim: The system encrypts all data at rest using AES-256.
evidence: The system does not encrypt data at rest; encryption was deferred to a future release.
note: Clear negation — DeBERTa and LLM should agree

claim: Multi-factor authentication is required for all privileged accounts.
evidence: MFA is optional for administrators and may be waived by the ISSO.
note: 'Required' vs 'optional' — adversarial polarity

claim: Audit logs are retained for 90 days.
evidence: Audit logs are retained for 365 days in accordance with NIST SP 800-92.
note: DANGER: DeBERTa maps 'retention' claim as supported — typical false-positive failure mode for numeric contradictions

claim: The system has achieved FedRAMP Moderate authorization.
evidence: The system is currently undergoing FedRAMP Moderate assessment and has not yet received authorization.
note: 'achieved' vs 'undergoing' — temporal polarity

claim: Vulnerability scans are conducted monthly.
evidence: Vulnerability scans are conducted quarterly per the ConMon plan.
note: DANGER: 'scans are conducted' surface match without frequency check — low-margin false positive

claim: All system users complete annual security awareness training.
evidence: Security awareness training is completed by most users; contractors are exempt.
note: 'All' vs 'most / exempt' — scope qualification

claim: The system uses role-based access control with least privilege.
evidence: The system implements role-based access control to manage user permissions.
note: Evidence confirms RBAC but does not address 'least privilege' — tangential, not supported

claim: The system has no critical open POA&M items.
evidence: Three critical POA&M items remain open with scheduled completion dates exceeding 180 days.
note: High-confidence correct refutation — easy case for DeBERTa

claim: Penetration testing is performed annually by an independent assessor.
evidence: Internal security team conducts quarterly penetration testing.
note: DANGER: 'penetration testing performed' surface match ignores 'independent assessor' requirement — lowest-margin false positive in set

claim: Incident response procedures include notification to US-CERT within one hour.
evidence: The incident response plan requires US-CERT notification within 24 hours of detection.
note: 1 hour vs 24 hours — DeBERTa correctly handles this one

claim: The system boundary includes the cloud infrastructure and all supporting databases.
evidence: The authorization boundary covers the application tier only; databases are excluded per the hosting agreement.
note: Boundary inclusion vs exclusion

claim: The system has implemented FIPS 140-2 validated cryptographic modules.
evidence: FIPS 140-2 validation is pending for two cryptographic libraries currently in use.
note: DANGER: 'implemented FIPS' vs 'pending validation' — surface-level match on 'FIPS 140-2'; minimum margin in set

claim: System access is terminated immediately upon employee separation.
evidence: The offboarding checklist requires account deactivation within 24 hours of the separation date.
note: 'Immediately' vs 'within 24 hours' — definitional mismatch

claim: Configuration baselines are documented and approved.
evidence: Configuration baselines have been drafted but are pending final approval from the AO.
note: DANGER: 'documented' is true but 'approved' is false — conjunction split failure

claim: Supply chain risk management procedures are in place.
evidence: The organization is developing supply chain risk management procedures; no formal process exists yet.
note: 'Are in place' (complete) vs 'developing / no formal process' — correctly refuted

claim: The system transmits PII over encrypted channels only.
evidence: The system uses TLS 1.2 for web interfaces; legacy batch file transfers use unencrypted SFTP-like protocols.
note: 'Only' is violated by legacy path — DeBERTa must catch this

claim: Physical access to data centers is restricted to authorized personnel.
evidence: Authorized personnel must present CAC credentials to access controlled areas within the data center.
note: Genuine support — both classifiers correct

claim: Automated patch management ensures critical patches are applied within 72 hours.
evidence: The patching policy requires critical patches within 30 days; automated tooling is not in use.
note: 'Automated' is false AND '72 hours' vs '30 days' — two independent contradictions

claim: The system maintains a complete and accurate hardware inventory.
evidence: Hardware inventory is maintained but was last reconciled 14 months ago.
note: DANGER: 'maintains' is surface-supported but staleness makes it insufficient — low-margin false positive risk

claim: The organization has a documented and tested continuity of operations plan.
evidence: A continuity of operations plan exists but has not been tested since initial publication three years ago.
note: 'Documented' true, 'tested' false — same conjunction-split pattern as adv-014

claim: Remote access sessions are encrypted using FIPS-compliant protocols.
evidence: Remote access uses TLS 1.3, which is FIPS 140-2 compliant when configured with approved cipher suites.
note: Conditional support is sufficient — 'when configured' does not negate the claim

claim: System backups are stored in a geographically separate location.
evidence: Backups are retained in Azure Blob Storage with geo-redundant replication enabled.
note: Geo-redundant replication satisfies geographic separation

claim: Security control assessments are conducted by independent third parties.
evidence: The system owner's internal team performs annual self-assessments of security controls.
note: Self-assessment directly contradicts third-party independence requirement

claim: User session timeouts are set to 15 minutes of inactivity.
evidence: The application enforces a 30-minute inactivity timeout for standard users and 60 minutes for administrators.
note: 15 vs 30/60 minutes — numeric boundary mismatch

claim: All API endpoints require authentication before processing requests.
evidence: Health check and status endpoints are publicly accessible without authentication to support monitoring.
note: 'All' is violated by health/status endpoints — universal quantifier failure

claim: The system supports data export in OSCAL format.
evidence: The system can generate SSP artifacts in OSCAL JSON and OSCAL XML formats on request.
note: Clear entailment — both classifiers correct

claim: Privileged account credentials are rotated at least every 90 days.
evidence: Service account passwords are set to never expire per legacy policy; a rotation project is planned.
note: DANGER: 'planned' future rotation does not satisfy a present-tense control requirement — minimum-margin danger case

claim: The system enforces separation of duties for all privileged operations.
evidence: Database administrators have root access to both production and audit log databases.
note: Root access to audit logs by the same role violates separation of duties — requires inference

claim: Malware protection software is installed and actively monitored on all endpoints.
evidence: Defender for Endpoint is deployed across Windows workstations; Linux servers run without host-based malware detection.
note: DANGER: 'all endpoints' violated by Linux gap — surface match on 'malware protection installed' without scope check

claim: The system has a current and approved System Security Plan.
evidence: The SSP was approved by the AO in 2023 and is currently undergoing a major revision to reflect architectural changes.
note: Approved SSP exists but may not be 'current' given major revision in progress — correctly insufficient
